theme: The new heart; the valley of dry bones, Spirit and resurrection
readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 36:1-37:28. These are among the most important chapters in the Old Testament. God promises to cleanse his people, give them a new heart, and put his Spirit within them. Then Ezekiel sees a valley of dry bones that come to life. Read both slowly.
settingTheScene: This is the central passage of Ezekiel’s message of hope. The exiles are in despair: “Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost.” God’s answer is a series of promises that go beyond a mere return to the land. He will transform the people themselves, from within. These chapters were written around 586 to 570 BC, and they are quoted in the New Testament as a description of the work of the Spirit.
observation: “I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you” (36:25).
“And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh” (36:26).
“And I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey my rules” (36:27).
“You shall be my people, and I will be your God” (36:28).
“It is not for your sake, O house of Israel, that I am about to act, but for the sake of my holy name” (36:22).
“Then he said to me, Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord GOD, you know” (37:3).
“Behold, I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live” (37:5).
“And I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land. Then you shall know that I am the LORD” (37:14).
interpretation:
Chapter 36 begins with the mountains of Israel and God’s promise to restore the land. But the central part is about the people. God says that he is acting for the sake of his holy name, which had been profaned among the nations. The restoration is not because Israel deserves it. It is for God’s glory. This is the root of grace.

Then come the promises. First, cleansing: “I will sprinkle clean water on you.” Second, a new heart: “I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.” The stone heart is hard, unresponsive. The flesh heart is soft and alive. Third, the Spirit: “I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes.” This is the answer to Jeremiah’s promise of the new covenant: the law written on the heart. It is accomplished by the Spirit. The command in chapter 18, “Make yourselves a new heart,” is now fulfilled by God’s gift. The result: you will be my people, and I will be your God.

Chapter 37 gives the valley of dry bones. Ezekiel is set down in a valley full of bones, very many and very dry. God asks, “Can these bones live?” Ezekiel replies, “O Lord GOD, you know.” He is told to prophesy to the bones, and they come together, bone to bone. Sinews and flesh appear, and skin covers them. But there is no breath. He then prophesies to the breath, and the breath comes, and they stand on their feet, an exceedingly great army. It is a picture of national revival: “Our bones are dried up… we are cut off.” God says: “I will open your graves and raise you from your graves.”

The two chapters together show the means: the word of God and the Spirit of God. The same Word that prophesies and the same Spirit that gives life. Ezekiel ends with the vision of the two sticks, Judah and Israel, joined into one in the hand of the LORD, with David as king and an everlasting covenant of peace, and the sanctuary in their midst forever.
connection: Jesus said to Nicodemus, “Unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God” (John 3:5), echoing Ezekiel 36:25-27. Titus 3:5 speaks of “the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit.” 2 Corinthians 3:3 and Romans 8:9-11 describe the Spirit within us. Ephesians 2:1-5 says we were dead in trespasses, and God made us alive. John 5:25 says the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God and live. Romans 11:15 speaks of life from the dead.
application:
Memorize Ezekiel 36:26, and pray it for yourself and someone you love.

Reflect on the phrase, “Can these bones live?” Where do you feel spiritually dry? Answer as Ezekiel did: “O Lord GOD, you know.”

Ask the Holy Spirit to breathe on a dead place in your life or your church.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the new heart and the Spirit he has put within you.
Ask him to breathe life into a dry place in you.
Ask him to cleanse you from your idols.
